record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: How should the temperature scale T* in manganites be characterized experimentally and theoretically, including whether d.c. resistivity shows anomalies at T*, whether the T* scales of cuprates and manganites reflect similar physics, whether specific heat develops structure from short-range order near T*, how T* depends on doping and tolerance factor, and whether the proposed mixed state between Tc and T* is qualitatively correct?

evidence.quote: The existence of the predicted new temperature scale T* above the Curie temperature should be further investigated. ... Are there anomalies in ρdc vs. temperature in Mn-oxides as well? Are the T* scales in cuprates and manganites indicative of similar physics? ... The dependence of T* with doping and tolerance factors should be analyzed systematically. ... Is the crude picture of the state between TC and T* shown in Fig.3 qualitatively correct?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the study of colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) manganites (mixed-valence perovskite oxides of the form R_{1-x}A_xMnO_3, with R a rare earth and A a divalent alkaline earth), theoretical and numerical studies of models combining double-exchange, superexchange, electron-phonon coupling, and quenched disorder predict the existence of a temperature scale T* lying above the ferromagnetic Curie temperature T_C, at which short-range correlated (clustered/inhomogeneous) states begin to form, while long-range ferromagnetic order only sets in at T_C. Characterize this scale T* both experimentally and theoretically by addressing the following:

(a) Does the d.c. resistivity ρ_dc(T) of manganites display detectable anomalies (e.g., changes of slope, inflection, or features distinct from the peak near T_C) at the temperature T*?

(b) Do the temperature scales denoted T* in hole-doped cuprate superconductors (the pseudogap onset) and in CMR manganites reflect physics of the same qualitative origin, in the sense of arising from a common mechanism of short-range correlated/clustered states above the long-range-ordering temperature?

(c) Does the specific heat C(T) develop measurable structure (a bump, shoulder, or enhanced entropy release) attributable to the onset of short-range order near T*?

(d) How does T*, and the separation T* − T_C, depend systematically on hole-doping concentration x and on the perovskite tolerance factor t = (r_A + r_O)/[√2 (r_Mn + r_O)] (which parameterizes the average A-site ionic radius and hence the Mn–O–Mn bond bending)?

(e) Is the qualitative picture in which, for T_C < T < T*, the system is an inhomogeneous mixture of ferromagnetic metallic clusters embedded in an insulating (e.g., charge/orbital-ordered or polaronic) background, correct as a description of the intermediate-temperature state of CMR manganites?

Provide a coherent characterization that answers (a)–(e) with definite theoretical predictions and corresponding experimental signatures.
artifact.status_search_result: The T* scale in manganites, associated with short-range ferromagnetic/polaronic correlations and nanoscale phase separation above T_C, remains an active and not fully settled topic. Experimental probes (small-angle neutron scattering, EXAFS, NMR, specific heat, optical conductivity) have detected precursor correlations above T_C, but a unified theoretical-experimental characterization, systematic doping/tolerance-factor dependence, and the conjectured analogy with the cuprate pseudogap are still debated in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Phase separation in manganites (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of nanoscale inhomogeneities and clustered states above T_C in CMR manganites, with predictions of a new scale T*.
status_evidence.claim: The T*/clustered-state picture in manganites is an actively investigated framework rather than a settled fact.

status_evidence.title: Polaron correlations above T_C in manganites
status_evidence.snippet: Neutron scattering observations of short-range polaron correlations developing well above the Curie temperature in CMR manganites.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental signatures consistent with a T* > T_C scale exist but their systematic doping/tolerance dependence is incomplete.
